On November 17, 2023, Marcus Chen, a 62-year-old patient, was admitted to Stanford Medical Center for a complex robotic-assisted laparoscopic kidney surgery. He was referred from his primary care physician with a diagnosis of a small renal mass in the lower pole of his right kidney.

Pre-operative imaging studies, including a contrast-enhanced CT scan and MRI, confirmed a 3.2 cm solid renal tumor with no evidence of metastatic disease. Mr. Chen was evaluated by the surgical team and determined to be an excellent candidate for minimally invasive surgical intervention.

The surgical procedure utilized the da Vinci Xi Surgical System, a state-of-the-art robotic surgical platform, allowing for precise and minimally invasive tumor resection. Dr. Samantha Rodriguez led the surgical team, performing a partial nephrectomy with meticulous attention to preserving renal function and maximizing oncological outcomes.

Operative Details:
- Procedure: Robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy
- Estimated blood loss: 125 mL

- Cervical collar immobilization for 6 weeks

- Comprehensive neurological evaluation: 3 months post-surgery

- Potential for incomplete fusion

Patient will be transferred to the orthopedic rehabilitation unit. Initial physical therapy will begin 24 hours post-surgery, focusing on:

3. Gait training with walker support

Patient Education Resources:
Comprehensive recovery guidelines available at: https://stanfordorthopedics.org/knee-replacement-recovery

- First outpatient physical therapy: April 12, 2023
- Comprehensive surgical follow-up: May 15, 2023

- Aspirin 81mg daily for DVT prophylaxis
